newsitem.title: UK: July Brent system throughput broadly stable - Shell.
newsitem.headline: July Brent system throughput broadly stable - Shell.

text.p: Brent system operator Shell Exploration and Production (Shell Expro) on Friday estimated North Sea Brent crude system throughput in July at 409,076 barrels per day (bpd), slightly higher than the 408,806 bpd pumped in June.
Shell Expro also confirmed it had postponed a maintenance shutdown of its 70,000 bpd Brent Bravo field originally due June 1-7 "until later in the year".
A spokeswoman said Shell was expecting to carry out the work in late August.
Average Brent pipeline throughput in the 12 months to the end of May was 445,445 bpd, Shell said.
Shell Expro is a joint venture between Royal Dutch/Shell Group and Exxon Corp.

Brent system throughput includes crude produced from 13 fields and several satellite wells piped to the Sullom Voe terminal in the Shetland Islands, where it is blended with Ninian crude and exported as Brent Blend.
Shell Expro said the throughput forecast was preliminary and may be "subject to significant fluctuation".
